title: Research
text: My research lies at the intersection of stochastic control, optimization, applied probability, and decision-making under uncertainty. A recurring theme in my work is the development of mathematical models and computational methods for systems operating under incomplete information, stochastic dynamics, or model uncertainty.

title: Research
section: Stochastic Control and Markov Jump Systems
text:
Stochastic Control and Markov Jump Systems
A substantial part of my research concerns dynamical systems subject to random regime changes, with particular emphasis on Markov jump linear systems and settings in which the underlying operating mode is only partially observed.
My work in this area addresses control, filtering, stability analysis, and detector-based methods for systems with incomplete mode information and stochastic switching. The main objective is to characterize how partial information affects the design and performance of controllers and estimators, while retaining formulations that are mathematically tractable and computationally implementable.

title: Research
section: Distributionally Robust Optimization and Decision-Making under Uncertainty
text:
Distributionally Robust Optimization and Decision-Making under Uncertainty
My current research also focuses on decision-making under model ambiguity, particularly in situations where the probability distributions governing a system cannot be assumed to be known exactly.
I study distributionally robust formulations in which uncertainty is represented through ambiguity sets around nominal probabilistic models. Topics of interest include KL-divergence ambiguity sets, optimization over probability distributions, robust policy design, and free-energy-based formulations of decision-making.
A central goal is to develop approaches that combine rigorous mathematical analysis with computational methods for nested optimization and worst-case probabilistic models.

title: Research
text:
Stochastic Games and Mathematical Finance
Another strand of my research concerns strategic decision-making under uncertainty, with applications to stochastic games and mathematical finance.
These problems involve interacting decision-makers facing stochastic economic or environmental conditions and naturally combine tools from stochastic control, game theory, optimal stopping, and free-boundary analysis.
Recent work in this direction studies strategic sustainable investment and the interaction between firms and investors when investment opportunities and economic conditions evolve randomly.
